title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Both WHO AND ECDC has been notified regarding a potential outbreak starting in April on MV Hondius cruise, that departed from South America and was on its way towards Europe on the Atlantic Ocean. Patient zero, died onboard ship on 11.04. Two additional deaths have occurred, including wife of patient zero and a German woman. Currently, 6 cases have been laboratory confirmed as Hantavirus andes infection, the only species within Orthohantavirus genus with previous evidence of ability to human - human transmission. One of the passengers, British national has been evacuated to South Africa in critical condition and on 2.05 PCR test for Hantavirus of his sample result came positive, pointing to potential outbreak. This mobilized South African authorities to test the wife of index patient body. The test also returned positive and on 4.05 WHO declared an outbreak. As of 13.05, all patients have been removed from the ship and repatriated. The current status is 8 confirmed cases, two possible, 1 inconclusive and 3 deaths [1-4].
After just 6 days upon first PCR result and 4 days after declaring an outbreak, first sequence has been publicaly released, from a Swiss resident that traveled the MV Hondius cruise [5]. So far, sequences of 5 isolates have been released and apart from Swiss isolate also include sequences from South African (n = 2) and Netherlands (n = 2) [6].
The aim of the phylogenetic analysis here is to characterize the strains isolated during the outbreak, assess their relatedness, estimate tMRCA, as well as identify potential adaptive mutations that could be associated with transmissibility or other features enhancing fitness of virus.

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Methods
First, to assess identity taxonomy of the Hantavirus isolates, phylogenetic placement was performed within broad variety of Orthohantavirus species, including members of old world Hantaviruses (Murinae such as Seoul virus, Arvicolinae such as Puumala virus). Strains were selected based on list specified charactarized previously by Jonsson et al [7]. The taxonomy was verified with virological taxonomy [8]. In the species specified in table 1 of [7], did not match ICTV classifical. For example some of the species such as Calabazo, there was no official ICTV classfication. Further, several species have been reclassfied. For instance, Rio Segundo virus taxa has been abolished after 2015. Also, some of the species were merged into single taxonomy, such as Bermejo virus, Pergamino virus, Lechiguanas virus, Maciel virus, Oran virus, Laguna Negra virus, Araraquara virus, Juquitiba virus which are all members of Ortohantavirus andense taxa. Selecion of strains was guided by self-determining rules: include representatives of both Old and New World Hantavirus taxa, strains with complete M segment sequence in Genbank category of NCBI virus were selected. If there was more than 1 sequence available for species, 2 sequences were selected, from different geographical locations, if possbible. For Orthohantavirus andes, 3 sequences were retrieved, one being an oubtreak strain. Upon selection, sequences were retried from NCBI virus in multi fasta format, as well as corresponding metadata in csv format. Sequences were aligned using MAFFT v7.526 [9] with –auto flag. Phylogenetic tree was inferred with IQTREE v3.1.1 [10] with multiple sequence alignment as input, while specifying -m MFP for sequence evolution model finding and -B 10000 for number of ultrafast bootrastraps. Phylogenetic tree was then visualized in R (Figure 1).

Result
The outbreak strain have been placed within Orthohantavirus andes species, with high clade bootstrap support value (97%) Figure 1, supporting the initial findings regarding the species of outbreak isolate [5].

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Methods
For phylogenetic analysis at the Orthohantavirus andes species level, sequences were retrieved from pathoplexus portal [6], for segment S, M and L. Sequences were filtered based on the known length range of each segment according to [11]. To account for variation, introduced during sequencing we allowed variation of +- 200 bp for each of the segmenty, which resulted in following length filtering criteria: S - 1.6-2.3 kb, M - 3.5-4 kb, L - 6.3-6.8 kb. Ultimately, 102, 87 and 76 sequences were obtained for segment S, M and L, respectively (accessed on 15.05.2026), in a raw multi fasta format. The sequences were aligned with MAFFT [9], with –maxiterate 1000 and –localpair parameters, followed by manual trimming in MEGA12 [12], to remove uneven 5’ and 3’ ends as well as grouped sites that have gaps in most of the sequences. PP_006W1UB.1 sequence was removed from M segment alignment due to significant amount of unknown nucleotides (N). After trimming, phylogenetic reconstruction was performed with IQTREE3 (10) for each segment alignment, with GTR+F+R2 sequence evolutionary model (best fit model, estimated by model finder), with 10000 ultrabootstraps. Phylogenetic trees were visualized in R.

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Results
The placement with sister clade is consistent across S, M, L segments Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 5, supporting no evidence of recombination, between different strains of Orthohantavirus andes. Outbreak samples (n = 5) form a monophylethic clade consisting of highly similar sequences, supporting possibility of single spillover event or multiple spillovers over short period of time (infection from common source). The most closely related sequences are: PP_006VZ4W.1 and PP_006VZ5U.1 , which correspond to NRC-3/18 and NRC-4/18, two cases from San Martin de Los (Andes, Neuquen, Argentina, near border with Chile) from 2018. San Martin de Los is located approximately by 2350 km road distance from Ushuaia, a location where cruise departed from, and even further from the islands where cruise stopped and where spillover also could potentially occur. Currently, there are no sequences, either from rodent or human Hantavirus andes isolates from southern Chile, Argentina or the islands where cruise stopped.
This highlights limited knowledge of Hantavirus andes phylogeography and therefore limited ability to answer the question of spatial origin of spillover, with currently available data.

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Methods
The trimmed alignment for each of the segments was used to derive pairwise SNP distances between all outbreak samples and sister clade samples. SNP distances were obtained with dist.dna function (R, package: ape). Networks were generated with graph_from_data_frame function (R, package: igraph).

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Results
SNP distance between outbreak strains and sister clade were equal to 22 SNPs for segment S Table 1, 35-36 SNPs for segment M Table 2 and 73-80 SNPs for segment L Table 3. When comparing outbreak strains, there were no mutations found in segment S @snp-network-s. For M segment 2 SNPs were found differ: between PP_006W6RC.2 and every other strain in outbreak @snp-network-m, consistent with branching above that isolate visible in phylogenetic tree Figure 5, suggesting 2 mutations occurred on the stem branch leading to the the clade containing the rest of outbreak isolates (PP_006WDKH.1, PP_006WBLH.2, PP_006W3U9.2, PP_006WDJK.1) For the segment L, the SNP distance between outbreak strains varies between 0-2 SNPs. The most basal isolates: PP_006WDJK.1 and PP_006WDKH.1 were found to differ by 1 SNP. PP_006W6RC.2 and PP_006W3U9.2 were found to differ by 1 SNP. PP_006W3U9.2 and PP_006WBLH.2 also differ by 1 SNP, while PP_006W6RC.2 and PP_006WBLH.2 have no differences in SNPs @snp-network-l.

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Molecular clock analysis

Methods
For molecular dating, sequences were re-downloaded from pathoplexus [6], including only ones having collection date available between 1995-01-01 and 2026-05-06, within length range: S - 1.6-2.3 kb, M - 3.5-4 kb, L - 6.3-6.8 kb. 38, 30 and 27 sequences were obtained for segment S, M and L, respectively. Sequences were aligned with mafft [9], specifying –maxiterate 1000 and –localpair parameters and the alignments were manually trimmed in MEGA12 [12] to remove 5’ and 3’ ragged ends. Blocks of missing sites within sequence alignment were removed. Sites with missing gaps for most or all sequences in alignment were also removed. Sequences PP 006W1TD.1|M, PP 006W1UB.1|M and PP_006W6RC.2|L were removed due to abudance of unknown base calls (Ns). Phylogenies were reconstructed using IQTREE3 [10], with -B 10000 and -m MFP. Tip dating was performed with treetime [13], specifying following parameters: –confidence –relax 1.0 0, –max-iter 100, –reroot least-squares –gtr infer.


Results
The dates spanned from 1996 to 2026 for segment S and from 1997 to 2026, for segments M and 1997 to 2026 Root to tip regression analysis showed temporal signal in segment S Figure 2 and segment M datasets, while segment L lacked measurable evolutionary signal. The estimated evolutionary rates was 3.480e-03 for segment S and “1.446e-03” for segment M, which correspond to 5.99 SNP per genome segment (0.00348 substitution per site x 1723 sites in alignment) and 5.06 SNP (0.001446 substitutions per site x 3501 sites), for segment S and M respectively. The obtained evolutionary rate values are consistent with known substitution rate ranges for Orthohantavirus andes [14].

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Methods
For molecular dating, sequences were re-downloaded from pathoplexus [6], including only ones having collection date available between 1995-01-01 and 2026-05-06, within length range: S - 1.6-2.3 kb, M - 3.5-4 kb, L - 6.3-6.8 kb. 38, 30 and 27 sequences were obtained for segment S, M and L, respectively. Sequences were aligned with mafft [9], specifying –maxiterate 1000 and –localpair parameters and the alignments were manually trimmed in MEGA12 [12] to remove 5’ and 3’ ragged ends. Blocks of missing sites within sequence alignment were removed. Sites with missing gaps for most or all sequences in alignment were also removed. Sequences PP 006W1TD.1|M, PP 006W1UB.1|M and PP_006W6RC.2|L were removed due to abudance of unknown base calls (Ns). Phylogenies were reconstructed using IQTREE3 [10], with -B 10000 and -m MFP. Tip dating was performed with treetime [13], specifying following parameters: –confidence, –max-iter 100, –reroot least-squares –gtr infer. We run time calibration multiple times with different parameters specified for different clock models (–relax 1.0 0 for uncorrelated relaxed clock, –relax 1.0 1.0 for correlated relaxed clock and no flag specified for strict clock) and coalescence models (–coalescent opt for costant, –coalescent skyline for skyline or no parameter specified). We estimated lower and upper bounds of tMRCA for the outbreak strains.

title: Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus Andes MV Hondius Cruise Outbreak in April - May 2026
text:
Results
The dates spanned from 1996 to 2026 for segment S and from 1997 to 2026, for segments M and 1997 to 2026 for segment L. Root to tip regression analysis results indicated temporal signal in segment S Figure 6 and segment M Figure 7 datasets, while segment L Figure 8 lacked measurable evolutionary signal. The estimated evolutionary rates was 3.480e-03 for segment S and 1.446e-03 for segment M, which correspond to 5.99 SNP per genome segment (0.00348 substitution per site x 1723 sites in alignment) and 5.06 SNP (0.001446 substitutions per site x 3501 sites), for segment S and M respectively Table 4. The obtained evolutionary rate values are consistent with known substitution rate ranges for Orthohantavirus andes [14]. The lower bound of tMRCA for segment S varies from 2009 to 2021 Table 5 and from 2010 to 2016 for segment M Table 6, depending on the model, while the upper bound is same for segment S (2026-04-25) despite model selected Table 5, and varies from 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-25 for segment M, depending on the coalescent and clock model combination Table 6. Given the characteristics of Hantavirus andes biology, which is characterized by incubation period ranging from 9 to 40 days, [15] with median of human-to-human incubation period of 20.1 days and 18.3 days rodent-to-human incubation period [16], the lower bound is too far in the past to be epidemiologicaly informative for this particular spillover event. The upper bound for segment M point out to March 2026, which considering infection biology of Hantavirus andes, is consistent with the time of symptom onset for probable patient zero which was on April 3 and history of 3-month travel in Argentina and Chile, prior to the boarding cruise [17].
